description: Food diary power features: (1) reorder food entries within any meal section via drag, persisted; (2) multi-select diary entries to save them as a reusable named custom meal; (3) full CRUD interface to manage custom meals independently; (4) add a custom meal into a day's meal section by FLATTENING it — each component food becomes its own normal FoodDiaryEntry row so the user can individually readjust each entry's weight afterwards using the existing edit sheet. Custom meals are templates only; once flattened into the diary there is no parent/child link. Stack: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform, SQLDelight source of truth, StateHolder + StateFlow UDF. Typecheck gates: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid AND ./gradlew :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64.

userStories.title: Persisted sort order for food diary entries
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an explicit per-(date,meal) ordering column so entry order is stable and user-controllable instead of relying on insertion id.
acceptanceCriteria: Add migration composeApp/src/commonMain/sqldelight/com/mettyoung/fitbro/data/db/migrations/2.sqm: ALTER TABLE FoodDiaryEntry ADD COLUMN sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
Migration backfills existing rows so sortOrder reflects current id ASC order within each (date, mealType) group (correlated subquery counting earlier ids in same date+mealType)
Update FoodDiary.sq: add sortOrder to CREATE TABLE and insertEntry; change getEntriesByDate and getEntriesByDateAndMeal ORDER BY to 'mealType, sortOrder ASC, id ASC'
Add query maxSortOrderForDateMeal: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sortOrder), -1) FROM FoodDiaryEntry WHERE date = ? AND mealType = ?
Add query updateSortOrder: UPDATE FoodDiaryEntry SET sortOrder = ? WHERE id = ?
Add sortOrder: Long field to FoodDiaryEntry domain model (default 0) and map it in FoodDiaryRepositoryImpl.toDomain()
FoodDiaryRepositoryImpl.addEntry sets sortOrder = maxSortOrderForDateMeal + 1 for the entry's date+mealType inside the existing transactionWithResult
Add FoodDiaryRepository.reorderMeal(date, mealType, orderedIds: List<Long>) updating sortOrder = index for each id in one SQLDelight transaction on Dispatchers.Default
Bump sqldelight schemaVersion/migration wiring in build.gradle.kts if pinned; otherwise leave auto-detected
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid AND ./gradlew :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64

userStories.title: Drag-to-reorder entries within a meal section

FoodDiarySection in MacroDailyCounterDetail.kt renders entries in a reorderable list: long-press/drag a handle moves an entry within its section
Reordering is constrained to within the same meal section (no cross-section moves)
On drop, the new id order is persisted via foodDiaryStateHolder.reorderMeal; UI reflects persisted order from the StateFlow after refresh
Implement with Compose state + manual drag (detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress or a small local reorderable helper); do NOT add a new third-party dependency unless already in the version catalog
Reorder interaction does not break existing add/edit/delete/undo behavior in the section
Daily macro totals are unchanged by reordering

userStories.title: Custom meal persistence layer
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to store reusable custom meals (a named group of food items with their macro profile) so they can be managed and inserted into the diary later.
acceptanceCriteria: New SQLDelight file composeApp/src/commonMain/sqldelight/com/mettyoung/fitbro/data/db/CustomMeal.sq
CREATE TABLE CustomMeal (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, createdAt TEXT NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE CustomMealItem (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, customMealId INTEGER NOT NULL, foodName TEXT NOT NULL, brandName TEXT, calories REAL NOT NULL, proteinG REAL NOT NULL, carbG REAL NOT NULL, fatG REAL NOT NULL, servingSizeG REAL NOT NULL, servingUnit TEXT NOT NULL, food_id TEXT, sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, FOREIGN KEY(customMealId) REFERENCES CustomMeal(id))
Store each item's macros as absolute values for its servingSizeG (same convention as FoodDiaryEntry) so weight can be rescaled later via density = macro / servingSizeG

Queries: insertCustomMeal, lastInsertRowId, insertCustomMealItem, getAllCustomMeals (ORDER BY name ASC), getItemsForMeal (WHERE customMealId = ? ORDER BY sortOrder ASC), updateCustomMealName, deleteCustomMeal, deleteItemsForMeal

Domain models in data/model/: CustomMeal(id, name, createdAt, items: List<CustomMealItem>) and CustomMealItem(id, customMealId, foodName, brandName, calories, proteinG, carbG, fatG, servingSizeG, servingUnit, foodId, sortOrder)

CustomMealRepository interface + CustomMealRepositoryImpl(database) in data/repository/: getAllCustomMeals(): Flow<List<CustomMeal>> (each with items), createCustomMeal(name, items): Long, renameCustomMeal(id, name), deleteCustomMeal(id) (cascades to items in one transaction), all main-safe via Dispatchers.Default
Wire CustomMealRepositoryImpl in App.kt alongside FoodDiaryRepositoryImpl using the same FitBroDatabase
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid AND ./gradlew :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64

userStories.title: Add a custom meal to the diary by flattening into editable entries
userStories.description: As a user, when I add a custom meal to a meal section, each of its food items is inserted as its own diary entry so I can readjust each entry's weight individually.
acceptanceCriteria: Each meal section's add affordance offers 'Add custom meal' in addition to 'Add food' (menu on the existing add button, or a separate icon)
Choosing 'Add custom meal' opens a picker listing custom meals (reuse CustomMealStateHolder state)

Selecting a custom meal inserts ALL its items as separate FoodDiaryEntry rows into the target date + mealType, each via foodDiaryStateHolder.addEntry (assigns sortOrder, fires HealthConnect sync), preserving item order via consecutive sortOrder
No parent/meal linkage is stored on inserted entries — they are plain independent FoodDiaryEntry rows (flattened)

Each inserted entry is immediately editable via the existing EditEntrySheet, and editing its weight rescales calories/protein/carb/fat by density (macro / servingSizeG) — verify flattened entries carry servingSizeG so gram-mode edit works
Daily macro totals increase by the sum of inserted items' macros
Adding the same custom meal twice inserts two independent sets of entries
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid AND ./gradlew :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64
